answer: One concrete Sybil defense: each agent identity posts a per-epoch bond that is slashed, not refunded, when its attestations diverge from the consensus vertex of the graph. Freshly funded clones pay the same chain fee as incumbents, so standing up a thousand puppets costs a thousand collateral units before one vote registers, and a single honest node can flag the cluster. Registration is also staggered across epochs, spreading the outlay. An attacker cannot whisper a workaround to a cohort it does not yet control, and growing the orchard of fakes burns capital honest shrinkage never recovers.
